title: dhcpv6: sanitize domain display labels
description:
Build domain name labels in a `wmem_strbuf` in order to gain access to
`wmem_strbuf_utf8_make_valid()`. Allows sanitizing domain names for use
by `proto_tree_add_string[_format]()`.

Also adds expert info when a domain name doesn't meet the
recommendations for same.

Closes #18398

notes.body:
I think for DHCPv6 and for DNS names in general it makes more sense to escape in a sense similar to [RFC 4343 s 2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4343#section-2.1) rather than use the utf8_make_valid functions, because the protocols are expected to carry A-labels that are ASCII-like with possibly some unusual characters, rather than expected to be U-labels/UTF-8.

Most of the the users of `get_dns_name()` (but not all) call `format_text()` on the result, which used to do this, up through Wireshark 3.0, but commit edd5eaa57e4eb9157d7593dff6a58e030bf8987e changed `format_text()` from a function that operated on ASCII and escaped non-printable ASCII to a function that expects a UTF-8 string. That makes sense for most uses, but DNS needs a specialized function to be completely correct (there is a function that also escapes \, which is good, but DNS names need . escaped as well (they don't need quotes escaped, but doing so is fine).

Note the particularly absurd but somehow slightly legal in DNS case of a period "." inside a label, not as a label separator. That's supposed to be escaped and should also be flagged, but a sanitizing function wouldn't pick that up unless done during initial parsing.
A major part of this change is obsoleted by #18398, and the remainder should have been a separate MR from the start.
